A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VICON study. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and relocated figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original fluid-prediction experiments, baseline comparisons, dataset-mixture ablations, rollout-stride analyses, and computational measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds patch-resolution experiments and a turbulence kinetic energy comparison.

M1.justification: The patch-based architecture, positional encodings, block-causal attention, training loss, normalization, and rollout procedures remain unchanged. Sections 4.2 and 4.5 clarify notation and explanation; the new patch-size experiments test configurations of the retained method.

E1.justification: Both versions use PDEArena-Incomp, PDEBench-Comp-LowVis, and PDEBench-Comp-HighVis for fluid prediction. The new turbulence diagnostic selects already-covered LowVis cases, and the patch study changes model configurations. No new experiment with incomplete or irregularly sampled inputs is reported.

E2.justification: MPP-B is relabeled MPP and explicitly identified as using AViT-B; it remains the same external comparator, including for the new turbulence diagnostic. Vanilla ICON is discussed as computationally infeasible, without an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds TKE mean absolute error evaluation on cases initialized with fully developed turbulence. Its new patch-resolution study tests sizes 8, 16, 32, and 64, reducing token/feedforward dimensions from 1024/2048 to 512/1024 for the finer configuration. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands supplementary validation with two new analysis areas: patch-resolution sensitivity across all three datasets (Figure 3) and turbulent-flow fidelity, including spatial predictions and error fields against MPP (Figure 4). The earlier dataset-mixture and rollout-stride analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2's new results retain point estimates and unbanded curves. The existing standard deviations concern normalization and error scaling.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports TKE MAE of 0.016 for VICON versus 0.049 for MPP, plus patch-resolution curves favoring size 16 under the tested configurations. Numerical results in Tables 1–3 and 8 and the existing stride curves remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 newly defines TKE using averaged squared velocity fluctuations and defines fluctuations relative to an equilibrium velocity. Existing operator definitions, Markov assumptions, attention and normalization equations, and appendix PDE equations are retained; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The introduction adds a contribution claim of approximately 67% lower TKE prediction error and explicitly claims robust rollout with incomplete or irregular temporal data. The original long-term L2 accuracy and computational-efficiency claims remain, while the title now explicitly calls VICON a foundation model.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the TKE comparison as evidence of better turbulent-flow preservation. It attributes finer-patch degradation partly to reduced hidden dimensions and adds explicit memory and 3D scalability limitations in Sections 5–6. Existing dataset-diversity and rollout interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 specifies the comparator's AViT-B architecture and documents dimension reductions and memory constraints for the new patch experiments, including infeasibility below 8 x 8 patches despite mixed precision. Existing appendix architecture, optimizer, hardware, and training-budget disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The revised introduction adds the practical qualification that explicit PDE information required by competing approaches may be unavailable or imprecise, sharpening the motivation for implicit context-based learning. The reference list and Related Works section otherwise retain the same coverage.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and headers, rewrites portions of the introduction and patch/rollout explanations, clarifies patch terminology, and adds an Impact Statement. The main section hierarchy and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds the patch-resolution and TKE figures. V1 Figures 3–4 are retained as appendix Figures 5–6, with resizing and revised captions. The overall layout and table structures remain similar, but Figure 6's new captions incorrectly reference the incompressible Equation 9 for compressible-flow examples.

improvement.justification: V2 adds a useful physical-fidelity diagnostic, experimental support for the patch choice, and explicit memory/3D limitations, improving evidence and qualification for the retained method. The improvement is limited by the patch study's simultaneous changes to model width and by newly introduced appendix caption-reference errors.
